11.text: I mentioned just now that among the Maritime Chukchee consideration

12.text: for old men is not so marked as among the reindeer-breeders. The life of

13.text: the maritime people is harder. Each morsel of food has to be obtained by

14.text: great exertion, by danger and hardship: therefore an old man, unable to get

15.text: his store of food himself, becomes a charge on other people. There is no

16.text: herd or other property worthy of much attention. The experience of an old

17.text: hunter does not count for much when he remains at home, and in times of

18.text: privation he is one too many to feed; therefore the old men whom I met

19.text: among the Maritime Chukchee looked dull and sad, nor were they as numerous

20.text: as among the Reindeer Chukchee. This was due perhaps to the hardships

21.text: of maritime life, the less active hunters being often unable to meet danger,

22.text: and thus losing their lives. The killing of old people, of which I shall speak

23.text: later on, probably originated among the Maritime Chukchee.¹

24.text: It seems that a similar difference, though less apparent, exists between

25.text: the Reindeer and the Maritime Koryak. Mr. Jochelson, in speaking of the

26.text: treatment of old people by the Koryak, remarks that among the Reindeer

27.text: Koryak the new form of household economy has developed the principle of

28.text: personal property more sharply.² In an oral communication he mentioned
28.note: Footnote marker keyed as superscript U+00B2 per keying_spec.md §2.10.

29.text: that in reality among the Reindeer Koryak the old men have more authority

30.text: than among the Maritime Koryak, because of their ownership of reindeer-

31.text: herds, which remains in their hands.

32.text: In recent times, property of value obtained in trade with American

33.text: whalers appeared even among the Maritime Chukchee. Almost every large

34.text: village has several traders, who go inland to the reindeer camps and barter

35.text: white men’s ware for skins and reindeer-meat. Some of them even have

36.text: storehouses of their own; others are poorer, and sometimes their capital is

37.text: small indeed. The owners of this property, though ever so old, continue to

38.text: hold it, and their position in life does not become lower with increasing age.
